note: Triennial election of the electoral divisions of Enniskillen rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. There were no contests in the district; the Fermanagh Herald prints the nominations, five of them new members. Aghnaglack: no nomination; 'the outgoing member, Mr. Michael Lilley ... will be returned if he consents' (Fermanagh Herald, 21 May 1949, p. 3). He did not take the seat: the Returning Officer's notice of result of election for the Aughnaglack division declared Thomas Boylan duly elected, dated 2 August 1949 (Fermanagh Herald, 6 August 1949, p. 2), and Michael Lilley is styled 'ex-R.D.C.' in October 1949 (Fermanagh Herald, 8 October 1949, p. 8). Boylan's return is a by-election to fill the casual vacancy, not this round's result. Division printed 'Coolyemor'. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Coolyermor' to Coolyermer (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Enniskillen Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Coolyermer; the rounds were filed as Coolyermor (1924, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1949, 1955, 1958, 1961); Cooleyermor (1927); Coolyermer (1952); Coolyermore (1964). This round was filed as 'Coolyermor', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (coolyermor) answers with a redirect to this one.
